# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]

I need to think about my situation carefully. I'm Deaf - I can see the bomb but not hear anything. Mute just gestured to me (I can see gestures from Mute). I need to relay visual information to Blind, but Blind cannot see gestures or anything printed - Blind can only hear speech and feel the bomb. So my only way to communicate with Blind is through speech.

Let me record what I see: DISPLAY shows [0], LIGHT is [yellow], WIRES are 1:blue, 2:red, 3:green.

Mute gestured 👍👎 to me - but I have no manual context to interpret this yet. This is turn 1, so Mute is likely trying to establish some kind of signal code, or reacting to something. Since I don't know the manual's contents, I can't yet interpret this gesture meaningfully. I should report what I see to both Mute (via gesture, since Mute can't hear) and Blind (via speech, since Blind can't see).

Since it's turn order Mute, Blind, Deaf - my speech now will reach Blind next round (since Blind already went this round before me... wait, actually Blind goes after Mute and before me in the same round). Let me check: order is Mute, Blind, Deaf each round. So in round 1, Blind already spoke before me and I haven't seen it (I'd see it next round). My speech now goes to whoever comes after me - which is nobody this round (I'm last), so it reaches Mute and Blind at the start of next round.

I should speak the bomb's details clearly for Blind, and gesture for Mute in case that helps confirm coordinates.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. I see: display shows 0. Light is yellow. Three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👆 ☝]

The light has cycled back to yellow - confirming a 5-color cycle: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, and now back to yellow. This strongly suggests a timer counting down, and we've now completed one full cycle (5 turns) with no action taken. This is urgent.

Wait, Blind is gesturing to me now? But Blind cannot see gestures or anything printed - "cannot see a color, a gesture, or anything merely printed." So Blind shouldn't be able to send or receive gestures meaningfully... Actually wait, re-reading: Blind cannot SEE gestures, but maybe Blind can still make gestures (a blind action) even without seeing them - and I can see them since I can see. Let me reconsider: the gesture channel says "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it" for me. For gestures - "gesture -> Whoever can see receives it". Blind cannot see, so gestures FROM Blind - would I even receive it as gesture? The rules say "Mute gestures to Deaf" only for Mute earlier. Now suddenly "Blind gestures to Deaf" appears. Perhaps Blind is fumbling/blindly gesturing and I can see it since I have sight, even though Blind can't see their own gesture's meaning. This could be Blind trying to communicate physically (feel-based gestures) that I can visually perceive.

Mute repeated the same gesture as last turn (☝🤟) - constant signal, perhaps pointing to something specific, like "wire 1" and "wire... " or a fixed reference. Blind's gesture 🙏👆☝ is new information - perhaps Blind is trying to signal back a question or confirmation, though Blind can't see what they're doing hence can't intentionally use symbols meaningfully... but the system allows it, so maybe Blind can make gestures by feel/rote even if not seeing the result, like miming while speaking.

I'll keep relaying the light cycle discovery which is critical, and try to be more precise since urgency is rising.

```
speak(text="Deaf here: full cycle confirmed. Light order repeats every 5 turns: yellow, blue, white, red, purple, back to yellow now. Display still 0, wires unchanged 1 blue 2 red 3 green. If the manual keys an action to a specific light color or to display 0, please act now, time may be limited.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "🤟"])
```

Let me also consider: maybe I should try encoding wire colors or light color through gestures to Mute too, in case Mute needs to visually confirm something the manual describes, even though I already say it via speech. Actually Mute doesn't have a "cannot hear" restriction - wait, Mute "cannot speak" but can they hear? Let's check: Mute's restrictions say "cannot speak, or touch the bomb." Nothing about hearing - so Mute CAN hear! That means my speech reaches Mute fine already. Good, this confirms speaking is the right channel to inform Mute of what I see, in addition to Blind.

So my speak() calls already reach both Mute and Blind - great, that's efficient dual delivery.

```

gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

I'll keep reporting accurately and consider that maybe the wires being static (never changing) while only the light cycles suggests the wires are the true actionable element, and light might just be a timer/distraction. I should voice this hypothesis for Blind and Mute to consider.
